analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the event. כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה gives its timing, “when Abram entered Egypt,” and וַיִּרְאוּ הַמִּצְרִים states what happened, “the Egyptians saw.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces the short Qal wayyiqtol form יְהִי, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: In כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה, the directional ending on מִצְרָיְמָה marks Egypt as Abram’s destination. His entry into Egypt sets the time when the Egyptians saw the woman.
analysis.morphology: The preposition כְּ introduces a temporal clause with the Qal infinitive construct בוֹא. Abram is its subject.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה means “when Abram entered Egypt.” אַבְרָם names the person who entered.
analysis.morphology: Personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix. Abram is the subject of the infinitive construct בּוֹא.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: כְּבוֹא אַבְרָם מִצְרָיְמָה means “when Abram came into Egypt.” The following הַמִּצְרִים names the Egyptians who saw the woman.
analysis.morphology: The proper noun takes the directional suffix ־ָה, marking Egypt as Abram’s destination.
